semantics.what: Detached human approval of the Superbee cutover roster and of the publication policy each reviewed target carries. release/targets.json stays the only place these values are written; this file records that a reviewer approved exactly that roster and exactly those values. It holds digests, never copies, so no policy value is declared in two places.
semantics.surface: Per target the approved digest covers: package name, allow_production, workflow_contract, tuple outcome, tuple production flag, and the full publication policy (npm_tag, npm_promote_tag, github_latest). Versions and tags are deliberately outside the digest - they move within an already-approved target and are governed by release/burned-versions.json, the functional successor floor, and the v<version> tag binding.
semantics.authority: Enrolling a target, retiring one, or moving a publication policy value in release/targets.json invalidates the approval recorded here and fails every load of the manifest. Re-approval is therefore a second, separately reviewed change to a second file: it cannot be smuggled in as a manifest edit.
semantics.lifecycle: The failure names each drifted target and prints both the approved digest and the digest the manifest now declares, alongside the exact surface that produced it. Re-approving means reading that surface, agreeing to it, and writing the declared digest here in the same reviewed commit as the manifest change.

review: PR #9 remediation, finding F6: roster and publication policy need an authority a manifest edit alone cannot satisfy.
